claim: INVS/NPHP2 is one of the over 25 NPHP genes identified to date.
source: INVS/NPHP2 is one of the over 25 NPHP genes identified to date.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract without specific citation, representing current understanding of NPHP genetics.

claim: Global knockout of Invs in mouse leads to renal fibrosis and cysts.
source: In mouse, global knockout of Invs leads to renal fibrosis and cysts.
evidence: This claim references prior work on Invs knockout mice, representing established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Epithelial-specific knockout of Invs in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant mice resulted in renal cyst formation and severe stromal fibrosis.
source: Epithelial-specific knockout of Invs in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant mice resulted in renal cyst formation and severe stromal fibrosis
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data presented in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice, where Invs is deleted in stromal cells, displayed no observable phenotypes up to the young adult stage.
source: Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice, where Invs is deleted in stromal cells, displayed no observable phenotypes up to the young adult stage
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased cell proliferation and myofibroblast activation occurred early during disease progression and preceded detectable cyst formation in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney.
source: Further, increased cell proliferation and myofibroblast activation occurred early during disease progression and preceded detectable cyst formation in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 2 and 3 showing markers at P7 before cyst formation.

claim: Concomitant removal of cilia partially suppressed the phenotypes of the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney.
source: Moreover, concomitant removal of cilia partially suppressed the phenotypes of the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6 comparing double mutants to single mutants.

claim: VPA reduced cyst burden, decreased cell proliferation and ameliorated kidney function decline in Invs mutant mice.
source: Finally, VPA reduced cyst burden, decreased cell proliferation and ameliorated kidney function decline in Invs mutant mice.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 7 showing effects of VPA treatment.

claim: Primary cilia are widely distributed cell surface organelles that function as signaling hubs for almost all vertebrate cell types.
source: Primary cilia are widely distributed cell surface organelles that function as signaling hubs for almost all vertebrate cell types (Schneider et al., 2005; Rohatgi et al., 2007; Lancaster et al., 2011; Huangfu et al., 2003; Haycraft et al., 2005; Corbit et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Ciliary dysfunction is associated with an array of human disorders, collectively termed ciliopathies, that include obesity, mental retardation, retinal degeneration, and polycystic kidney disease.
source: Ciliary dysfunction is associated with an array of human disorders, collectively termed ciliopathies, that include obesity, mental retardation, retinal degeneration, and polycystic kidney disease (PKD), among many others (reviewed in Hildebrandt et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Disruption of cilia biogenesis almost inevitably leads to the formation of epithelium-lined fluid filled kidney cysts in mouse.
source: Disruption of cilia biogenesis almost inevitably leads to the formation of epithelium-lined fluid filled kidney cysts in mouse (Pazour et al., 2000; Yoder et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Polycystin 1 and 2 are targeted to cilia and this specific trafficking highly correlates with their in vivo function.
source: Polycystin 1 and 2 (PC1 and PC2), encoded by the autosomal dominant PKD (ADPKD) genes Pkd1 and Pkd2, respectively, are targeted to cilia and this specific trafficking highly correlates with their in vivo function (Yoder et al., 2002; Barr and Sternberg, 1999; Cai et al., 2014; Pazour et al., 2002; Yoshiba et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Concomitant removal of cilia ameliorates cyst progression triggered by polycystin inactivation.
source: Interestingly, although both cilia biogenesis and polycystin mutants develop cystic kidney, concomitant removal of cilia ameliorates cyst progression triggered by polycystin inactivation, demonstrating that intact cilia are required for cyst growth in ADPKD models (Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Polycystins function to inhibit a novel and uncharacterized cilia-dependent cyst activating (CDCA) signaling pathway.
source: Based on these results, it was postulated that polycystins function to inhibit a novel and uncharacterized cilia-dependent cyst activating (CDCA) signaling pathway (Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis postulated based on prior work, as indicated by the citation.

claim: Nephronophthisis (NPHP) is a recessive renal cystic disease with cysts mostly confined in the corticomedullary junction region in the juvenile form of the disease, and more widely distributed across the kidney in the infantile form.
source: Nephronophthisis (NPHP) is a recessive renal cystic disease with cysts mostly confined in the corticomedullary junction region in the juvenile form of the disease, and more widely distributed across the kidney in the infantile form.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about NPHP disease characteristics.

claim: NPHP is considered as a ciliopathy.
source: Since multiple NPHP proteins are localized to cilia, basal bodies and/or show functional involvement in cilia biogenesis and/or signaling, NPHP is considered as a ciliopathy (Fliegauf et al., 2006; Otto et al., 2003; Otto et al., 2008; Shiba et al., 2010; Shiba et al., 2009; Williams et al., 2010; Winkelbauer et al., 2005; Won et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: A prominent feature of NPHP is the severity of interstitial fibrosis compared with other types of renal ciliopathies.
source: Compared with other types of renal ciliopathies, a prominent feature of NPHP is the severity of interstitial fibrosis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about NPHP disease characteristics.

claim: At least 25 genes have been identified for the classic form of NPHP.
source: Genetically NPHP is highly heterogenous and at least 25 genes have been identified for the classic form of this disease (for a review, see Srivastava et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a review article.

claim: Mouse mutants of NPHP genes do not always show obvious renal phenotypes.
source: However, mouse mutants of NPHP genes do not always show obvious renal phenotypes (Won et al., 2011; Jiang et al., 2008; Ronquillo et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Invs was discovered as a novel gene inactivated in a mouse mutant with reversed internal organ asymmetry along the left-right body axis.
source: Invs, the homolog of which is associated with both infantile and juvenile NPHP in human, was discovered as a novel gene inactivated in a mouse mutant with reversed internal organ asymmetry along the left-right body axis and was originally named as Inversin (Invs) (Yokoyama et al., 1993; Mochizuki et al., 1998; Morgan et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The whole-body Invs knockout model displays kidney cysts in both the medulla and cortex and renal fibrosis at the neonatal stage, resembling the renal phenotypes of infantile NPHP.
source: This whole-body knockout model additionally displays kidney cysts in both the medulla and cortex and renal fibrosis at the neonatal stage, resembling the renal phenotypes of infantile NPHP (Morgan et al., 1998; Phillips et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: At P7, the mutant kidney size was comparable to that in control animals and there was no significant difference in body weight and kidney to body weight (KBW) ratio between the two groups.
source: At postnatal day 7 (P7), the mutant kidney size was comparable to that in control animals and there was no significant difference in body weight and kidney to body weight (KBW) ratio between the two groups (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: At P14, the mutant kidneys were larger, and KBW ratios were significantly increased, although the body weight remained comparable.
source: At P14, the mutant kidneys were larger, and KBW ratios were significantly increased, although the body weight remained comparable (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Mutant kidneys became increasingly enlarged at P21 and P28, with comparable body weight at P21 and reduced body weight in mutants at P28.
source: Mutant kidneys became increasingly enlarged at P21 and P28, with comparable body weight at P21 and reduced body weight in mutants at P28 (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: No significant differences in KBW ratios were detected between genders in either control or mutant groups at P14 and P21.
source: We additionally compared KBW ratios between male and female mice and no significant differences were detected between genders in either control or mutant groups at P14 and P21 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: No cyst was detected in the P7 mutant kidney and the cystic index remained comparable between the wild type and mutant kidney.
source: Consistent with the progression of the KBW ratio, no cyst was detected in the P7 mutant kidney and the cystic index remained comparable between the wild type and mutant kidney (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: At P14, small cysts were detected, and the cystic index was already significantly increased in the mutant kidney.
source: At P14, small cysts were detected, and the cystic index was already significantly increased in the mutant kidney (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: At P21, cysts became larger and more numerous in mutant kidneys.
source: At P21, cysts became larger and more numerous in mutant kidneys (Figure 1E)
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: By P28 mutant kidneys were severely cystic with large cysts throughout the cortex and medullar region.
source: by P28 mutant kidneys were severely cystic with large cysts throughout the cortex and medullar region (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The cystic index progressively increased in mutant kidneys from P7 to P28.
source: The cystic index progressively increased in mutant kidneys during the same time window (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Neither the collecting duct nor the proximal tubule showed enlargement at P7.
source: Consistent with histology, neither the collecting duct, labelled with Dolichos Biflorus Agglutinin (DBA), nor the proximal tubule, labelled with Lotus Tetragonolobus Lectin (LTL), showed enlargement at P7 (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: At P14, cysts were detected mostly in the DBA positive collecting duct.
source: At P14, cysts were detected mostly in the DBA positive collecting duct (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: At P21 and P28, DBA positive cysts were enlarged and numerous.
source: At P21 and P28, DBA positive cysts were enlarged and numerous (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Large cysts were detected in the thick ascending limb, labelled by anti-Tamm-Horsfall protein (THP) at both P21 and P28.
source: Large cysts were also detected in the thick ascending limb, labelled by anti-Tamm-Horsfall protein (THP) at both P21 and P28 (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The LTL positive proximal tubule was free from cysts at P28.
source: By contrast, the LTL positive proximal tubule was free from cysts at P28 (Figure 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: At P7, mutant and control mice were comparable in BUN levels.
source: At P7, mutant and control mice were comparable (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by BUN data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: At P14, BUN levels became significantly higher in mutant mice.
source: At P14, BUN levels became significantly higher in mutant mice (Figure 1I)
evidence: This claim is supported by BUN data shown in Figure 1I.

claim: BUN levels became more elevated in mutant mice at P21 and P28, demonstrating a progressive decline of kidney function.
source: and BUN levels became more elevated in mutant mice at P21 and P28, demonstrating a progressive decline of kidney function (Figure 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by BUN data shown in Figure 1I and represents an inference about kidney function.

claim: An increase of collagen deposition was detected in the cortex region of mutant kidneys at P21.
source: In mutant kidneys, an increase of the blue staining of collagen was detected in the cortex region (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by trichrome staining data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: SMA signal was increased in the cortex region of the mutant kidney at P14 and became dramatically elevated and widespread in the mutant kidney at P21 and P28.
source: SMA signal was increased in the cortex region of the mutant kidney at P14 and became dramatically elevated and widespread in the mutant kidney at P21 and P28 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Vimentin signal was increased in the cortex region of the mutant kidney at P14 and P21.
source: Vimentin signal was increased in the cortex region of the mutant kidney at P14 and P21 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: At P9, the KBW ratio was normal in mutants.
source: At P9, the KBW ratio was normal in mutants (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: At P9, SMA and vimentin signal in the cortex region was already increased.
source: By contrast, SMA and vimentin signal in the cortex region was already increased (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Isolated tubule dilation was detected on mutant kidney sections at P9.
source: However, we also detected isolated tubule dilation on mutant kidney sections (Figure 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: At the non-cystic P7 stage, SMA and vimentin signals were modestly increased in the cortex region.
source: At the non-cystic P7 stage, SMA and vimentin signals were modestly increased in the cortex region (Figure 2F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: RT-qPCR using kidney lysates showed a significant increase of Sma and Vimentin mRNA level in the mutant at P7.
source: Reverse transcription and quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) using kidney lysates also showed a significant increase of Sma and Vimentin mRNA level in the mutant at P7 (Figure 2G).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: PCNA positive cells increased in the collecting duct in the cortex region of the mutant kidney at P7.
source: PCNA positive cells increased in the collecting duct (DBA+) in the cortex region of the mutant kidney (Figure 3A and B, upper panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The number of proliferating interstitial cells was significantly increased in the mutant kidney at P7.
source: The number of proliferating interstitial cells, outside of epithelial regions encircled by laminin, was significantly increased in the mutant kidney (Figure 3A and B, lower panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The number of cells in interphase and S phase was significantly increased in both the collecting duct and interstitium at P7.
source: we further showed that the number of cells in interphase and S phase, respectively, was significantly increased in both the collecting duct and interstitium (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The number of mitotic cells was significantly increased in both the collecting duct and interstitium at P7.
source: Moreover, the number of mitotic cells, labelled by the mitosis marker phosphorylated histone H3 (pHH3), was significantly increased in both regions (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Foxd1-Cre drives Cre expression in metanephric mesenchymal cells destined to be stromal cells, including interstitial cells, mesangial cells and pericytes.
source: Foxd1-Cre drives Cre expression in metanephric mesenchymal cells destined to be stromal cells, including interstitial cells, mesangial cells and pericytes; and Cre activity can be readily detected at E11.5, similar to the onset of Cdh16-Cre activity (Shao et al., 2002a; Shao et al., 2002b; Hum et al., 2014; Humphreys et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work characterizing Foxd1-Cre.

claim: At P28, no differences were seen in kidney size, KWB ratio, cyst formation, or collagen deposition in the Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mutant kidney.
source: At P28, we did not observe any morphologic or functional phenotypes. No differences were seen in kidney size, KWB ratio, cyst formation, or collagen deposition in the mutant kidney at P28 (Figure 4A–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A-E.

claim: Immunostaining of SMA failed to detect any changes in the Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mutant kidney at P28.
source: Moreover, immunostaining of SMA failed to detect any changes in the mutant kidney at P28 (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: BUN levels were normal in P28 Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mutants.
source: In accordance, BUN levels were also normal in P28 mutants (Figure 4H).
evidence: This claim is supported by BUN data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Wide expression of eGFP-Cre was detected in the renal stroma in both the cortex and medulla region of Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice.
source: We first analyzed the expression of eGFP-Cre by immunostaining of eGFP and detected wide expression of eGFP-Cre in the renal stroma in both the cortex and medulla region (Figure 4I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: INVS was detected in the proximal compartment of 85.01% of cilia in cells from control kidneys.
source: We detected INVS in the proximal compartment of 85.01% of cilia in cells from control kidneys, consistent with the previously reported localization pattern of INVS (Shiba et al., 2009; Bennett et al., 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4J and K and is consistent with prior work.

claim: Only 34.24% INVS-positive cilia were observed in cells of Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mutant kidneys.
source: whereas only 34.24% INVS-positive cilia were observed in cells of mutant kidneys (Figure 4J and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claim: ANKS6 was detected in 87.78% of cilia in cells from the control kidney.
source: Similarly, ANKS6, encoded by another NPHP gene and is known to localize to the Inversin compartment in a INVS dependent manner (Bennett et al., 2020; Czarnecki et al., 2015), was detected in 87.78% of cilia in cells from the control kidney
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4J and K and is consistent with prior work.

claim: ANKS6 was reduced to 39.89% cilia in cells from the Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mutant kidney.
source: but was reduced to 39.89% cilia in cells from the mutant kidney (Figure 4J and K)
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4J and K.

claim: At P56, Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice showed normal body weight, KBW ratio, renal histology and BUN, suggesting normal kidney structure and function.
source: At P56, Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice showed normal body weight, KBW ratio, renal histology and BUN, suggesting normal kidney structure and function (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: INVS is localized to and defines the Inversin compartment, a proximal segment of cilia.
source: INVS is localized to and defines the Inversin compartment, a proximal segment of cilia (Shiba et al., 2009; Bennett et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: INVS is also detected in subcellular locations outside of the cilium.
source: However, it is also detected in subcellular locations outside of the cilium (Nürnberger et al., 2004; Nürnberger et al., 2002; Estrada Mallarino et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: INVS is dispensable for cilia biogenesis.
source: Moreover, INVS is dispensable for cilia biogenesis (Phillips et al., 2004; Sang et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: At P21, cilia were present in cyst-lining DBA positive cells in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney.
source: At P21, cilia were present in cyst-lining DBA positive cells as indicated by immunostaining with the cilia marker anti-acetylated tubulin in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: ARL13B localization to the cilium was undisrupted in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney.
source: In addition, ARL13B localization to the cilium was also undisrupted (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Cilia biogenesis is disrupted in both Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre knockout and Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre knockout kidney.
source: Immunostaining with the cilia marker anti-acetylated tubulin confirmed abrogation of cilia in the distal nephron in both Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single knockout and Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double knockout mice, as expected (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single knockout mice showed a slower progression of renal cystic disease in comparison to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants.
source: Consistent with previous reports, Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single knockout mice showed a slower progression of renal cystic disease in comparison to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison to prior work and data in the current study.

claim: At P21, neither kidney size nor KBW ratio were significantly changed in Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants compared to age matched control mice.
source: At P21, neither kidney size nor KBW ratio were significantly changed in Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants compared to age matched control mice (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidneys contained only small cysts but a significant increase of cystic index at P21.
source: In histological sections, Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidneys contained only small cysts but a significant increase of cystic index (Figure 5F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: Stage-matched Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants had enlarged and severely cystic kidneys, with significantly increased KBW ratios and cystic index at P21.
source: By contrast, stage-matched Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants had enlarged and severely cystic kidneys, with significantly increased KBW ratios and cystic index (Figure 5D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5D-G.

claim: The increase of the KBW ratio and cystic index was reduced in Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant mice in comparison to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant mice regardless of gender.
source: Interestingly, the increase of the KBW ratio and cystic index was reduced in Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant mice in comparison to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant mice regardless of gender (Figure 5E–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5E-G.

claim: The BUN level was significantly lower in Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutants than in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants regardless of gender, suggesting a partial suppression of kidney function decline.
source: Moreover, the BUN level was also significantly lower in Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutants than in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants regardless of gender, suggesting a partial suppression of kidney function decline (Figure 5H).
evidence: This claim is supported by BUN data shown in Figure 5H and represents an inference about kidney function.

claim: The increase of SMA and vimentin was more moderate in Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants compared to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants at P21.
source: Immunostaining of kidney sections revealed that the increase of of SMA and vimentin was more moderately in Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants compared to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutants showed reduced signal of SMA and vimentin compared to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants at P21.
source: In addition, Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutants showed reduced signal of SMA and vimentin compared to Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutants (Figure 5I).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5I.

claim: The levels of SMA and Collagen I were significantly increased in Invs single mutants compared to controls at P21.
source: While the levels of both proteins were significantly increased in Invs single mutants compared to controls
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The levels of SMA and Collagen I in double mutants were significantly reduced compared to Invs single mutants at P21.
source: Moreover, the levels of SMA and Collagen I in double mutants were significantly reduced compared to Invs single mutants (Figure 5J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5J.

claim: At P21, 0.9% of DBA positive collecting duct cells were PCNA positive in the control kidney.
source: At P21, 0.9% of DBA positive collecting duct cells were PCNA positive in the control kidney
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: 6.3% of DBA positive collecting duct cells were PCNA positive in the Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney at P21.
source: which was increased to 6.3% in the Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: 22.9% of DBA positive collecting duct cells were PCNA positive in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney at P21.
source: and 22.9% in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: In the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney, 13.4% of DBA positive cells were PCNA positive, a significant decrease from the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant at P21.
source: In the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney, 13.4% of DBA positive cells were PCNA positive, a significant decrease from the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: In the cortex region of the control kidney, 2.1% of interstitial cells were PCNA positive at P21.
source: In the cortex region of the control kidney, 2.1% of interstitial cells were PCNA positive.
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: In the Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney, 7.2% of interstitial cells were PCNA positive at P21.
source: In the Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney, this number increased to 7.2% (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: 22.3% of interstitial cells were PCNA positive in the cortex of the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney at P21.
source: 22.3% of interstitial cells were PCNA positive in the cortex of the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre kidney
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: PCNA positive interstitial cells reduced to 12.8% in the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney at P21.
source: which reduced to 12.8% in the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: The level of PCNA, CDK1, and cyclin D1 was increased in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney at P21.
source: Results showed that the level of PCNA, CDK1, a kinase required for cell cycle progression, and cyclin D1, which is essential for cell proliferation and prevents cells enter quiescence, was increased in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The level of cyclin D1 was increased in the Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney at P21.
source: The level of cyclin D1, but not CDK1, was also increased (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The level of PCNA, CDK1 and cyclin D1 in the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney was significantly decreased in comparison to the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant kidney at P21.
source: the level of PCNA, CDK1 and cyclin D1 in the Invsflox/flox;Ift88flox/flox;Cdh16-Cre double mutant kidney was significantly decreased in comparison to the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre single mutant kidney (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: There was no difference in ciliary localization of PC2 between Invs-/- mutant and control mIMCD3 cells.
source: Immunostaining with anti-PC2 and the cilia marker anti-acetylated tubulin showed no difference in ciliary localization of PC2 between mutant and control cells (Figure 6E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6E and F.

claim: Pkhd1-Cre directs Cre expression in the collecting duct starting at E14.5, later than the onset of Cdh16-Cre expression.
source: Pkhd1-Cre directs Cre expression in the collecting duct starting at E14.5, later than the onset of Cdh16-Cre expression (Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: In Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mice, mutant kidneys were enlarged and cystic, with a significantly increased KBW ratio, cystic index and BUN level in both male and female mice and decreased body weight at P28.
source: In Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mice, mutant kidneys were enlarged and cystic, with a significantly increased KBW ratio, cystic index and BUN level in both male and female mice and decreased body weight at P28 (Figure 7A–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7A-E.

claim: VPA treatment decreased the size of the mutant kidney, but had no impact on body weight, in comparison to vehicle-treated mutants.
source: Results showed that this regiment of VPA treatment decreased the size of the mutant kidney, but had no impact on body weight, in comparison to vehicle-treated mutants (Figure 7A, B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: The KBW ratio, cystic index of kidneys and the BUN level in mutant mice were reduced significantly by VPA treatment in comparison to vehicle-treated mutants.
source: In addition, the KBW ratio, cystic index of kidneys and the BUN level in mutant mice were reduced significantly by VPA treatment in comparison to vehicle-treated mutants (Figure 7B–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7B-E.

claim: VPA treatment led to a more moderate level of myofibroblast activation in the cortex region of the mutant kidney.
source: Moreover, VPA treatment led to a more moderate level of myofibroblast activation in the cortex region of the mutant kidney, as indicated by the level of SMA (Figure 7F).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The kidney size, KBW ratio, cystic index and BUN level were not significantly affected by VPA treatment in control mice.
source: By contrast, the kidney size, KBW ratio, cystic index and BUN level were not significantly affected by the same VPA treatment in control mice, suggesting that mutant mice are selectively sensitive to VPA treatment (Figure 7A, B, D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7A, B, D and E and represents an inference about selective sensitivity.

claim: The reduced body weight phenotype in mutant mice was not suppressed by VPA treatment.
source: However, the reduced body weight phenotype in mutant mice was not suppressed by VPA treatment (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The number of PCNA positive cells in the collecting duct and the interstitium was reduced significantly by VPA treatment.
source: The number of PCNA positive cells in the collecting duct labeled by DBA and the interstitium outside of tubular regions outlined by anti-laminin signal was reduced significantly by VPA treatment (Figure 7G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7G and H.

claim: The abnormally increased level of PCNA, CDK1, and cyclin D1 in mutant kidneys was decreased significantly by VPA treatment.
source: The abnormally increased level of PCNA, CDK1, and cyclin D1 in mutant kidneys was decreased significantly by VPA treatment (Figure 7I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 7I and J.

claim: Defective epithelial cells are the main driver of NPHP phenotypes in Invs mutants.
source: Combined, our results suggest that defective epithelial cells are the main driver of NPHP phenotypes in Invs mutants, highlighting the significance of epithelial-stromal cross-talks in the development and progression of interstitial fibrosis in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing epithelial and stromal knockout models.

claim: The fibrotic response is triggered before cyst formation by signals from defective epithelial cells in the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre model.
source: Our results showed that SMA and vimentin is already upregulated at P7, before detectable cyst formation, suggesting that the fibrotic response is triggered before cyst formation by signals from defective epithelial cells in this model.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the time course analysis of fibrotic markers and cyst formation.

claim: INVS functions to signal terminal differentiation of renal epithelial cells and Invs mutant cells fail to exit cell cycle to enter the quiescent stage.
source: An attractive model is that INVS functions to signal terminal differentiation of renal epithelial cells and Invs mutant cells fail to exit cell cycle to enter the quiescent stage.
evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the observed increase in proliferation.

claim: INVS is specifically localized to a proximal segment of the cilium dubbed the Inversin compartment.
source: Previous work suggests that INVS is specifically localized to a proximal segment of the cilium dubbed the Inversin compartment (Shiba et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: INVS is localized to a novel fibril-like structure in the Inversin compartment.
source: Super-resolution imaging revealed that INVS is localized to a novel fibril-like structure in the Inversin compartment (Bennett et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: INVS interacts with multiple infantile NPHP proteins, including NPHP3, ANKS6 and NEK8.
source: Moreover, INVS interacts with multiple infantile NPHP proteins, including NPHP3, ANKS6 and NEK8; and is required for concentrating these proteins to the Inversin compartment (Shiba et al., 2009; Czarnecki et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: INVS is found in the plasma membrane, mitotic spindle and stress granule.
source: On the other hand, INVS is dispensable for cilia biogenesis and is also found in the plasma membrane (Phillips et al., 2004; Nürnberger et al., 2002), mitotic spindle (Nürnberger et al., 2004) and stress granule (Estrada Mallarino et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ift88 inactivation partially reduced cell proliferation, suppressed the severity of renal cyst and fibrosis, and improved kidney function in Invs mutants.
source: Significantly, Ift88 inactivation partially reduced cell proliferation, suppressed the severity of renal cyst and fibrosis, and improved kidney function in Invs mutants.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings from the double mutant experiments.

claim: Similar to polycystins, INVS functions to inhibit a cilia-dependent pro-cystic and pro-fibrotic pathway.
source: This result suggests that, similar to polycystins, INVS functions to inhibit a cilia-dependent pro-cystic and pro-fibrotic pathway (Figure 7K).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double mutant experiments and comparison to polycystin studies.

claim: In human, mutations in Inversin compartment genes are associated with the infantile form of NPHP.
source: Interestingly, genes encoding Inversin compartment components seem to form a unique functional module among the many NPHP genes. In human, mutations in Inversin compartment genes are associated with the infantile form of NPHP.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about human genetics of NPHP.

claim: In mouse, Anks6, Invs, Nphp3, and Nek8 mutants develop kidney cysts.
source: In mouse, Anks6, Invs, Nphp3, and Nek8 mutants develop kidney cysts, while mutants of several other NPHP genes show no obvious kidney phenotypes (Won et al., 2011; Jiang et al., 2008; Ronquillo et al., 2016; Morgan et al., 1998; Phillips et al., 2004; Czarnecki et al., 2015; Bergmann et al., 2008; Liu et al., 2002; Omran et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: NPHP is a major cause of ESRD in children and young adults.
source: NPHP is the most frequent monogenic cause of end stage renal disease (ESRD) in children and young adults (Hildebrandt et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Currently directed therapy is lacking for NPHP.
source: Currently directed therapy is lacking for NPHP.
evidence: This is stated as current clinical knowledge.

claim: The vasopressin V2 receptor antagonists OPC31260 and Tolvaptan have been shown to partially suppress phenotypic progression in Nphp3pcy mutant mice.
source: Although the vasopressin V2 receptor antagonists OPC31260 and Tolvaptan have been shown to partially suppress phenotypic progression in Nphp3pcy mutant mice, no directed therapy has been established for this disease (Aihara et al., 2014; Gattone et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: VPA reduces cell proliferation, slows down the progression of disease phenotypes and partially preserves renal function in Invs mutant mice.
source: In this study, we show that the pan HDACI VPA reduces cell proliferation, slows down the progression of disease phenotypes and partially preserves renal function in Invs mutant mice.
evidence: This is a summary of the primary findings from the VPA treatment experiments.

claim: At least four new HDACIs have been approved by FDA to treat lymphomas.
source: For example, at least four new HDACIs have been approved by FDA to treat lymphomas (Cappellacci et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: VPA is a drug that has been used to treat epilepsy with a known safety profile.
source: In addition, VPA is a drug that has been used to treat epilepsy with a known safety profile.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge.

claim: The epithelial-stromal crosstalk plays a significant role in the development of NPHP phenotypes in Invs mutants.
source: Epithelial-specific knockout of Invs in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant mice resulted in renal cyst formation and severe stromal fibrosis, while Invsflox/flox;Foxd1-Cre mice, where Invs is deleted in stromal cells, displayed no observable phenotypes up to the young adult stage, highlighting a significant role of epithelial-stromal crosstalk.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison of epithelial and stromal knockout phenotypes.

claim: There is a significant interaction of cilia and Invs function in vivo.
source: Moreover, concomitant removal of cilia partially suppressed the phenotypes of the Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutant kidney, supporting a significant interaction of cilia and Invs function in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the double mutant experiments.

claim: Renal epithelial cilia play a critical role in NPHP.
source: Our results reveal the critical role of renal epithelial cilia in NPHP and suggest the possibility of repurposing VPA for NPHP treatment.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: VPA could potentially be repurposed for NPHP treatment.
source: Our results reveal the critical role of renal epithelial cilia in NPHP and suggest the possibility of repurposing VPA for NPHP treatment.
evidence: This is a suggestion based on the experimental findings with VPA treatment.

claim: The reduction of body weight at P28 in Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mice in comparison to control mice was more moderate than that in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mice.
source: At P28, the reduction of body weight in Invsflox/flox;Pkhd1-Cre mice in comparison to control mice was more moderate than that in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mice (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Over-proliferation of epithelial cells is a driver of cyst progression.
source: Since over-proliferation of epithelial cells is a driver of cyst progression (Nadasdy et al., 1995; Takakura et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Vimentin is a marker of activated fibroblasts that becomes upregulated early during injury responses in the kidney.
source: We additionally performed immunostaining of vimentin, a marker of activated fibroblasts that becomes upregulated early during injury responses in the kidney (Ó hAinmhire et al., 2019; Zhou et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: ANKS6 is known to localize to the Inversin compartment in a INVS dependent manner.
source: Similarly, ANKS6, encoded by another NPHP gene and is known to localize to the Inversin compartment in a INVS dependent manner (Bennett et al., 2020; Czarnecki et al., 2015)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ift88 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT) gene essential for cilia biogenesis.
source: Ift88 is an intraflagellar transport (IFT) gene essential for cilia biogenesis (Pazour et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The cystic region in Invsflox/flox;Cdh16-Cre mutants was consistent with the expression domain of Cdh16-Cre.
source: Overall, the cystic region was consistent with the expression domain of Cdh16-Cre.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the immunostaining data showing which tubule segments were cystic.
